language_shifts.shift: Overview language softened: 'will enable us to maintain' becomes 'primarily will enable us to maintain' inserting a new qualifier; boilerplate reworded from 'softening the negative impact of the current challenging global economic environment' to 'position us well to overcome economic challenges' signaling a shift to more defensive framing

'Food safety' disappears from the named end-market list (present Q1-Q3, absent Q4-Q6) with no explanation; 'exceptionally diverse range of end markets' reduced to 'diverse range of end markets'; description changes from 'meet customer needs' to 'designed to meet our customers needs'; energy storage moves to first position in end-market list

Phrase shifts from 'the current challenging global economic environment' to 'a challenging global economic environment' — removal of 'current' implies challenges may be structural rather than transient; sales growth decelerated sharply to 3% from 14-16% in Q4-Q5 but Outlook language is near-identical copy of Q5 with no acknowledgment of the growth deceleration

red_flags: Greenbushes expansion commissioning commitment made in Q1 2017 ('Commissioning of the expansion is expected to begin in the second quarter of 2019 and would more than double the current lithium carbonate capacity') is never mentioned again in Q2-Q6 filings — topic dropped entirely with no follow-up status
Revenue growth decelerated from 14-16% in Q4-Q5 2018 to 3% in Q6 2018 yet Outlook language in Q6 is unchanged from Q5 — no updated forward-looking guidance or acknowledgment of material slowdown

Q5 ASR commitment described as 'expected to be completed in the third quarter of 2018' was delivered (Q6 confirms completion) but was immediately followed by announcement of a new $250M ASR in August 2018 — capital return structured as rolling program yet presented quarter-by-quarter as discrete commitments
CORFO quota request (Q3 2017) described as targeting 125,000 MT/yr lithium carbonate equivalent; approved in Q4 2018 at 145,000 MT/yr — upward revision not flagged as a change from original request

new_risks.risk: International revenue concentration quantified for the first time, elevating transparency of geographic dependency
new_risks.key_phrase: approximately 73% of our sales to foreign countries

new_risks.risk: International operations risk elevated to lead risk factor position, signaling increased management attention to geopolitical and trade-policy exposure
new_risks.key_phrase: Our substantial international operations subject us to risks of doing business in foreign countries, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations

escalated_risks.risk: Competition from Chinese market participants — previously a sub-bullet within competition risk, now embedded in expanded international operations risk with added trade-sanctions and export-control framing
escalated_risks.prior_language: our products are facing increasing competition from market participants in China
escalated_risks.current_language: foreign countries may adopt other restrictions on foreign trade or investment, including currency exchange controls; trade sanctions could result in losing access to customers and suppliers in those countries

escalated_risks.risk: International operations risk — scope broadened with quantified revenue exposure and elevated to lead position
escalated_risks.prior_language: Our substantial international operations subject us to risks of doing business in foreign countries...We conduct a substantial portion of our business outside the United States.
escalated_risks.current_language: Our substantial international operations subject us to risks of doing business in foreign countries...We conduct a substantial portion of our business outside the U.S., with approximately 73% of our sales to foreign countries. In addition, we operate and/or sell our products to customers in approximately 100 countries.

disappeared_risks.risk: Adverse conditions in the economy and volatility and disruption of financial markets — the lead standalone risk factor in the 2017 filing
disappeared_risks.likely_reason: reorganized — macroeconomic risk subsumed into expanded international operations risk section; no longer featured as a discrete opening risk

disappeared_risks.risk: Irregularities in demand for HPC catalysts and agrichemicals as a distinct standalone risk factor addressing specific product-cycle volatility
disappeared_risks.likely_reason: materialized/reorganized — PCS segment merged into Catalysts segment effective January 1, 2018; agrichemicals exposure reduced via divestitures; risk folded into general business risk disclosures

contradictions.target_claim: we became a leading integrated and low cost global producer of lithium and lithium compounds used in lithium-ion batteries for electronic devices, alternative transportation vehicles and energy storage technologies, meeting the significant growth in global demand for these products
contradictions.competitor_claim: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc. is a world-leading Industrial Gases company in operation for over 75 years...in fiscal year 2018 we had sales of $8.9 billion, assets of $19.2 billion, and a worldwide workforce of approximately 16,300 full- and part-time employees

corroborations.claim: Energy storage and clean energy solutions driving strong demand in specialty chemicals end markets
corroborations.evidence: Sales of $8,930.2 increased 9%, or $742.6, from underlying sales growth of 7% and favorable currency impacts of 2%. The underlying sales growth was primarily driven by higher volumes across all regional Industrial Gases segments

corroborations.claim: Refinery customers requiring continuous investment in catalysts and clean fuel technologies
corroborations.evidence: Air Products is also the world's leading supplier of liquefied natural gas (LNG) process technology and equipment...we began to execute our gasification strategy with the completion and onstream of the Lu'AN acquisition and our announcements of the Jazan gasifier/power project in Jazan, Saudi Arabia

corroborations.claim: Target's claim that alternative fuel and emissions control technologies represent expanding business opportunities
corroborations.evidence: We delivered operating margin of 22.0% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 34.9%...Highlights for 2018 Sales of $8,930.2 increased 9%...driven by higher volumes from base business growth and new, large industrial gas project onstreams

topics_dropped: Food safety as a named end market — present in end-market list Q1-Q3 2017, dropped starting Q4 2018 with no explanation
Tianqi Lithium partnership and Rockwood Lithium GmbH ownership structure — discussed in Q1 only, never revisited
Greenbushes expansion commissioning timeline — announced Q1 2017 as expected Q2 2019, never mentioned in Q2-Q6
Specific crude oil price characterization ('significantly lower crude oil prices') referenced in Q1 Outlook, replaced by generic 'crude oil price fluctuation' framing from Q2 onward

notable_shifts.observation: Most specific Outlook language across the series: explicitly names 'significantly lower crude oil prices', 'diverse energy storage needs', and 'cutting edge catalysts and technology by our refinery customers' as distinct market dynamics; food safety named as an end market; boilerplate uses superlative 'exceptionally diverse range'

First notable qualifier inserted: 'primarily will enable us to maintain leading market positions' replaces unconditional 'will enable'; closing boilerplate reworded from 'softening negative impact' to 'overcome economic challenges and to take advantage of future opportunities' — increased defensive posture

Food safety dropped from end-market list without explanation; 'exceptionally diverse' removed; energy storage promoted to first position in end-market list, signaling strategic pivot; Outlook adds PCS segment reorganization disclosure but reduces market-specific forward commentary to generic language

Outlook section is near-identical formulaic repetition of Q4 with no new forward-looking specifics despite 16% revenue growth quarter; management provided no quantitative guidance or new strategic milestones

Sales growth collapsed to 3% vs 14-16% in Q4-Q5 but Outlook language copied from Q5 unchanged; subtle but telling shift from 'the current challenging global economic environment' to 'a challenging global economic environment' removes temporal qualifier implying challenges are now structural; no specific forward guidance provided despite material growth deceleration
